## Maintenance

Every plugin released so far, by when it last shipped any version: in the six
months up to that month, six months to two years before, or not in two years.

```{python}
#| renderings: [light, dark]
show(plots.plugin_status(data.plugin_status()))
```

The same, as a share of all plugins:

```{python}
#| renderings: [light, dark]
show(plots.plugin_status(data.plugin_status(), share=True))
```

## The plugin template

New plugins made from the [napari-plugin-template](https://github.com/napari/napari-plugin-template)
(cookiecutter until mid-2024, copier since), found from each plugin's repo and
PyPI description.

```{python}
#| renderings: [light, dark]

```

## napari downloads

```{python}
by_system = data.pypi_downloads_by_system()
last12 = by_system[by_system["month"] > by_system["month"].max() - pd.DateOffset(months=12)]
all12 = last12["downloads"].sum()
desktop12 = last12[last12["system"].isin(["Windows", "macOS"])]["downloads"].sum()
```

napari was downloaded `{python} f"{all12 / 1e6:.1f}"` million times from PyPI in
the last twelve months, `{python} f"{desktop12 / 1e3:,.0f}"` thousand of them on
Windows or macOS. Most of the rest is Linux: CI and cloud machines, with
one-month spikes of a million or more. Windows and macOS follow people
installing napari themselves, so that is what's plotted. Data:
[ClickHouse's public PyPI dataset](https://clickpy.clickhouse.com/dashboard/napari).

```{python}
#| renderings: [light, dark]
desktop = by_system[by_system["month"] >= "2021-01-01"]
show(plots.pypi_downloads_desktop(desktop))
```
